title: Vision-based pursuit and formation control
description: Nonlinear model predictive control connects smooth target pursuit with camera centring and useful viewing geometry for UAV teams.
introduction: A UAV's motion determines what its camera can see. This work plans feasible pursuit motions that keep a target in view and studies how a team can maintain a useful formation around it.

problem.heading: Tracking depends on where the camera moves.
paragraphs: A target estimate alone does not determine a useful pursuit motion. The robot must move smoothly while preserving an informative view, rather than allowing the target to drift out of the camera image.
For a team, the relative positions of the UAVs also influence viewing geometry. Coordinating those positions adds a formation-control problem to the task of following a moving target.

approach.heading: Plan motion around the target and the view.
paragraphs: A nonlinear model predictive controller generates smooth, feasible pursuit motions. Camera centring is part of the control objective, connecting the target's image position with how the UAV moves.

The cooperative formulation coordinates UAV positions to maintain a formation and useful viewing geometry. The published evaluation separates this multi-UAV simulation study from the physical single-UAV experiment.

evidence.label: Multi-UAV pursuit and formation
evidence.text: The paper's multi-UAV pursuit and formation-maintenance evaluation is simulation-based. It studies coordinated behaviour and viewing geometry for a UAV team.

evidence.label: Single-UAV field experiment
evidence.text: The supplied outdoor demonstration uses one UAV. It supports the physical pursuit implementation without being presented as a hardware validation of cooperative team formation.
